subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw accept requester-owned outbound-only per-agent A2A allowlists as the public config contract, or require target-side receive/per-capability policy before landing this PR?
rationale: The PR changes cross-agent session authorization and adds a public config surface, so automation cannot choose the long-term least-privilege boundary safely.

options.title: Approve outbound-only after repairs
options.body: Accept requester-owned semantics, then require exact-ID normalization, changelog removal, conflict refresh, and focused validation before merge.

options.title: Require broader authorization first
options.body: Pause this branch and fold the work into a bidirectional or per-capability session authorization design before exposing new config.

options.title: Keep as discussion only
options.body: Leave the PR open for design discussion but do not land a public config contract until the broader per-agent scoping issue is resolved.

recommendation.title: Approve outbound-only after repairs
recommendation.body: Accept requester-owned semantics, then require exact-ID normalization, changelog removal, conflict refresh, and focused validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available owner from the inspected history because they merged recent session-visibility hardening and this decision is about that authorization boundary.
